pr_title: Fix multiple accounts being unable to verify with the same website
pr_body:
This pull requests fixes #20259 - a bug that restricted only the first account linked on a website to being verified. 

Before, if you had multiple accounts and wanted to verify multiple ones with a website, Mastodon would only verify the first one. Now, if you have multiple accounts, Mastodon will check every link on the page to see if any of them link back to your profile.
pr_comments: This looks to be specifically a `mastodon.social` issue. I will be closing this pull request.

issue_context.title: Unable to link multiple Mastodon accounts to single website
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Setup [website](https://jbmagination.com) with verification `rel="me"` for two accounts ([@JBMagination@mastodon.social](https://mastodon.social/@JBMagination) and [@JBMagination2@mastodon.social](https://mastodon.social/@JBMagination2))
2. Attempt to add website to both accounts
3. Only one (from my experience, the first on the page) will be verified


### Expected behaviour

Both accounts that I setup should be verified

### Actual behaviour

Only [@JBMagination2@mastodon.social](https://mastodon.social/@JBMagination2) is verified

### Detailed description

It appears that verification is only applied to one account, and the others are ignored even if on the same page. This has the potential to affect brands who want to have multiple accounts on an instance, as well as journalists and the like, who may in the future use a verified link to a trusted site like `washingtonpost.com` to prove their identity.

### Specifications

Mastodon 4.0.0rc1 (on https://mastodon.social)
comments:
it is because this line only checks the first matching link points back https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/cd0a87f170f795f3d2eeaadc06d6039aca395049/app/services/verify_link_service.rb#L36 so at the time of verifying you have to be first on the page.
I think you can verify one after another, (as a workaround right now) as long as at the time of saving the profile the link that points back is the first one with rel=me in it.

Just to confirm I understand the current behaviour, I think it will already allow multiple links to be verified if any are perfect match (i.e. someone copied and pasted the link and their server just got on and served it). If there are rel=me links but none of them are a perfect match then it will resolve the first one and see where it goes (for link shorteners).
So the non-working scenario is multiple link-shortened rel=me links if you are not the first one on the page. This does seem like it is already a good compromise, it does allow multiple people to verify the same page, but doesn't allow anyone bad to craft a page with a zillion rel=me links on it and have a mastodon server follow them all.
I'm going to close this because my issue is resolved, but also I'm leaning towards this being a mastodon.social issue.

review_comments: Ah. I think this was a fix for Twitter putting t.co links on their profiles back when they still added `rel=me` on their page. However, your change basically sends a request to every link on the page! That's a lot of requests and a lot of time.

Would there be a way to filter for this more efficiently? 

Assuming that this wants even links that redirect to Mastodon to be accounted for, then I'm not sure how else this can be done without getting rid of the fix. 

It also looks like the first condition might not be applied properly, considering in my case both accounts were linked to `https://mastodon.social` on the website - which looks like it should be applying to the first condition and making it true - but this condition is what's causing my failure.

Wait, no - this would only send a request to every `rel="me"` link on the page, as is defined in line 29:
https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/b303eacb9be49ed9ba9300b4c6b38be22f91aaec/app/services/verify_link_service.rb#L29

If you *did* have a lot of `rel="me"` links on your page, this still definitely would take up a lot of requests and time (so perhaps stop after 10 links?).
Could  link_redirects_back first check to see if test_url is already equal to @link_back before trying the request to resolve any link shorteners? Is there any downside to not following the link?

Links are already tested for exact match in the `links.any? { |link| link['href'].downcase == @link_back.downcase }` line of `link_back_present?`, so `link_redirects_back?` is only called when there is no direct match.
That being said, this checks for `https://instance.tld/@:username`, while `https://instance.tld/users/:username` is also a valid URL for that user. Maybe both should be checked.
